# Institute for Law Teaching and Learning

> A comprehensive resource for law school educators sharing innovative teaching methods, assessment strategies, and curriculum approaches for modern legal education.

Based at the University of Arkansas Little Rock Bowen School of Law, the Institute for Law Teaching and Learning provides faculty resources, pedagogical guidance, and practical exercises for law professors. The site features contributions from educators across multiple law schools including Gonzaga University, University of Connecticut, and LSU Paul M. Hebert Law Center.

## Key Topics

- Legal Education
- Teaching Methods
- Classroom Engagement
- Assessment Strategies
- Case Law Analysis
- Legal Writing
- ChatGPT and AI in Law
- Curriculum Reform
- Faculty Development
- Low-Tech Assessment
- Student Assessment
- Professional Development
- Law School Resources
- Doctrinal Classes
- Pandemic Teaching

## Teaching Methods & Classroom Engagement

- [Using Silent Signals to Assess and Engage the Students](https://lawteaching.org/2021/10/05/using-silent-signals-to-assess-and-engage-the-students): Classroom engagement technique using silent signals by Emily Grant and Sandra Simpson
- [Going Back to the Basics, Low-Tech Assessment Methods in Large Doctrinal Classes](https://lawteaching.org/2022/02/09/going-back-to-the-basics-low-tech-assessment-methods-in-large-doctrinal-classes): Low-tech assessment methods for large doctrinal classes by Sandra Simpson
- [Using the Local News as the Basis for an In-class Exercise](https://lawteaching.org/2022/01/04/using-the-local-news-as-the-basis-for-an-in-class-exercise-2): In-class exercise using local news for environmental law by Andrea Need
- [Instructional Check-Ins To Surmount Trials And Tribulations Of The Pandemic In The Era Of Meta Connection](https://lawteaching.org/2022/01/18/instructional-check-ins-to-surmount-trials-and-tribulations-of-the-pandemic-in-the-era-of-meta-connection): Pandemic teaching strategies and student check-ins by Lécia Vicente at LSU Paul M. Hebert Law Center

## Legal Writing & Research Skills

- [Writing Case Briefs](https://lawteaching.org/2021/11/16/writing-case-briefs): Guide to writing case briefs for first-year law students by Andrew Henderson
- [Looking Beyond Headnotes: Distinguishing Cases (Exercise)](https://lawteaching.org/2021/11/02/looking-beyond-headnotes-distinguishing-cases-exercise): Legal research exercise on case distinguishing and headnotes by Matthew Boles

## Technology & Innovation in Legal Education

- [ChatGPT Exercise in the LRW Class](https://lawteaching.org/2023/02/13/chatgpt-exercise-in-the-lrw-class): ChatGPT implications for legal writing classrooms by Sandra Simpson and Ashley B. Armstrong

## Core Resources

- [Institute for Law Teaching and Learning](https://lawteaching.org): Homepage for Institute for Law Teaching and Learning at University of Arkansas Little Rock Bowen School of Law
